items.stem: The specification says that diverse phenomena can be described in terms of a small number of key ideas. Which statement best describes a key idea in physics?

options.text: A way of thinking that recurs in many topics and describes a wide range of phenomena
An especially large and detailed topic that has to be revised in far more depth
A rule that applies only inside the topic in which it was first taught
A page of background reading that is never used in any examination paper

items.why: A key idea is valuable because it applies across the whole subject, not because it is detailed.

items.stem: The key ideas are of universal application and are embedded throughout the subject content. What does this mean for the examinations?

options.text: They are printed for teachers and are never examined in any paper
They can be assessed in questions on any topic, on all papers
They are examined only in questions set for the higher tier
They are not examined, as they are not a taught topic

items.why: The specification states that the key ideas underpin the assessment and are assessed across all papers.

items.stem: Which of the following does the specification list as a key idea in physics?

options.text: Learning the names of all the required practical activities
Quoting every calculated answer to three significant figures
The use of models, such as the particle model of matter
Recalling the names of the SI base units in physics

items.why: The specification lists the use of models, as in the particle model of matter or the wave models of light and of sound.

items.stem: Why is the particle model of matter called a model?

options.text: Because it is a physical copy of matter built for classroom use
Because it is an idea that no evidence has yet been found for
Because it applies to solids but not to liquids or gases
Because it is a simplified way to explain and predict

items.why: A model is a simplified representation judged by how well it explains and predicts.

items.stem: Light and sound are both described using a wave model. Which statement about these two models is correct?

options.text: Sound and light are both modelled as transverse waves through matter
Sound is modelled as a longitudinal wave and light as a transverse wave
Sound and light are both modelled as transverse waves on a screen
Each wave model is a real wavy object, like a small model plane

items.why: The two wave models differ: sound oscillates along the direction of travel, light across it.

items.stem: A car on a straight road has a constant resultant force acting forwards. Using the idea of cause and effect, what is the effect of that force?

options.text: The car keeps moving at a steady speed while the force acts
The car gains mass steadily while the force is applied
The car accelerates for as long as the force acts on it
The car halts the instant the force is removed

items.why: A resultant force is the cause and acceleration is the effect.

items.stem: A sample of an unstable isotope emits alpha particles. Applying the idea of cause and effect, what is the cause of this emission?

options.text: A chemical reaction between the outer electrons
The high temperature of the material around it
A collision with a nearby moving atom
A change inside the nucleus of the atom

items.why: The specification links changes in atomic nuclei to radioactive emissions.

items.stem: Two magnets repel each other without touching. Which group of effects does physics analyse using the idea of a field?

options.text: Electrical, magnetic and gravitational effects
Gravitational, frictional and elastic contact effects
Electrical, magnetic and thermal conduction effects
Magnetic, elastic push and near-contact effects

items.why: The specification names these three as the effects analysed using the field concept.

items.stem: Which statement correctly applies the key idea that differences are the drivers of change?

options.text: Gas flows out of a cylinder when the gas inside has a large volume
Energy is transferred by heating when an object is at a high temperature
Charge flows through a resistor when there is a potential difference across it
Charge flows through a resistor when a large charge is stored in the cell

items.why: Potential difference is the electrical case of a difference driving a change.

items.stem: The weight of an object is directly proportional to its mass. What does this tell you?

options.text: A graph of weight against mass is a straight line with a positive intercept
Weight and mass are the same quantity written in different units
The graph is a straight line, which by itself proves the two are proportional
Doubling the mass doubles the weight in the same gravitational field

items.why: Proportionality means the two quantities change by the same factor, with g as the constant.

items.stem: A student loads a spring with increasing weights and finds that extension is directly proportional to force. Which statement about this model is correct?

options.text: Doubling the force doubles the extension up to the limit of proportionality
Doubling the force doubles the extension for every force applied to the spring
Any straight-line graph shows extension is directly proportional to force
Doubling the force still doubles the extension even past the elastic limit

items.why: The proportional model holds only within a stated range of validity.

items.stem: The specification says that physical laws and models are expressed in mathematical form. Which statement shows this key idea?

options.text: Rearranging an equation changes the physical law that it describes
weight = mass × gravitational field strength is a relationship
An equation is only a shortcut for doing the arithmetic quickly
A description of a law in words is more precise than an equation

items.why: The equation expresses the law that weight is proportional to mass, in the form the specification uses.
